title: Variance Bound by Maximum Influence
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability distribution $\pi$, and suppose the real-valued functions on $\Omega$ have a finite nonempty orthonormal basis for the $\pi$-weighted inner product that includes the constant-one function. For any $n$, let $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$ take only the values $-1$ and $1$, and let $T$ be a randomized decision tree computing $f$. Then the variance of $f$ under the product distribution with marginal $\pi$ is at most the maximum coordinate influence of $f$ times the average cost of $T$ under that product distribution.
hypotheses_covered: There is a finite nonempty index set for the basis, with decidable equality
The basis is a real vector-space basis of functions on $\Omega$, has a constant-one basis vector, and is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
$T$ is a randomized decision tree computing $f$ for every seed
